record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does there exist a chiral polytope whose monodromy group on flags, generated by the involutions r_i that send a flag to its i-adjacent flag, is not a string C-group?

evidence.quote: Problem 3 Is there a chiral polytope whose monodromy group is not a string C-group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a unique minimum element and unique maximum element, in which every maximal totally ordered subset (flag) has exactly n+2 elements (so elements naturally receive ranks 0,1,...,n-1 between the minimum and maximum), every flag has, for each i in {0,1,...,n-1}, a unique i-adjacent flag differing from it only in its rank-i element, P is strongly flag-connected, and P satisfies the diamond condition. The polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

For each i in {0,1,...,n-1}, let r_i be the permutation of the set of flags of P that sends every flag to its i-adjacent flag. Each r_i is an involution. The monodromy group (also called the connection group) of P is the subgroup Mon(P) = ⟨r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1}⟩ of the symmetric group on the flags.

A string C-group of rank n is a pair (G, {s_0,...,s_{n-1}}) where G is a group generated by involutions s_0,...,s_{n-1} satisfying:
 (1) (s_i s_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i-j| ≥ 2 (the string condition), and
 (2) the intersection property: for all subsets I, J ⊆ {0,...,n-1}, ⟨s_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨s_j : j ∈ J⟩ = ⟨s_k : k ∈ I ∩ J⟩.

Question: Does there exist a chiral abstract polytope P such that the monodromy group Mon(P), with its distinguished generating set {r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1}}, is not a string C-group?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on the monodromy/connection group of chiral polytopes and the string C-group property did not surface a definitive resolution. It is known that the monodromy group of any abstract polyhedron (rank 3) is a string C-group (Hartley–Hubard–Pellicer–type results), and there is recent work constructing 4-polytopes whose connection groups fail to be string C-groups in the non-chiral setting, but no clear evidence that the question has been settled specifically for chiral polytopes was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of state of theory of abstract chiral polytopes with a list of open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem in a survey on chiral polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy Groups and Self-Invariance (Hubard, Orbanić, Weiss)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monodromy groups of abstract polytopes including chiral ones.
status_evidence.claim: Monodromy groups of chiral polytopes are an active area of investigation, with no general result identifying them as string C-groups.

status_evidence.snippet: Appendix listing open problems on abstract chiral polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference still lists problems about monodromy groups of chiral polytopes among open questions.
